source.author: verg
source.text: ter frustra comprensa manus effugit imago, par levibus ventis volucrique simillima somno.
source.text_original: ter frustra comprensa manus effugit imago, / par levibus ventis volucrique simillima somno.
source.text_english: Three times the image, seized in vain by the hand, escaped, like the light winds and most like fleeting sleep.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: anima enim cum diuortium fecit a corpore, est, ut ait idem poeta, par leuibus uentis uolucrique simillima somno, quia spiritus est et ipsa tenuitate incomprehensibilis, sed nobis, qui sumus corporales, deo autem, cui subiacet posse omnia, comprehensibilis.
reuse.text_original: anima enim cum diuortium fecit a corpore, est, ut ait idem poeta, par leuibus uentis uolucrique simillima somno, quia spiritus est et ipsa tenuitate incomprehensibilis, sed nobis, qui sumus corporales, deo autem, cui subiacet posse omnia, comprehensibilis.
reuse.text_english: For when the soul has parted from the body, it is, as the same poet says, most like sleep borne on gentle winds, because it is a spirit and, by its very subtlety, beyond grasp; but to us, who are bodily, it is beyond grasp, whereas to God, to whom the power over all things belongs, it is comprehensible.
